gaps.summary: The esg_policy property is richly populated for some companies (Primark) but empty for others (Analog Devices Inc), so entity coverage of sustainability commitments is uneven.
gaps.reproducibleQuery: entity_retrieval on 7a17ad96-4bbf-474f-a6e9-1cf4e5da84e3 with properties [esg_policy, employee_count] returns neither.
gaps.detail: Workaround: fall back to knowledge_search for the company's commitments, which did return a well-sourced answer for Analog Devices.

gaps.summary: Cala models the corporate parent (Analog Devices Inc) but not the Irish operating site in Limerick as its own entity, so Mid-West presence cannot be read from the graph.
gaps.reproducibleQuery: entity_search 'Analog Devices' returns the US parent and foreign subsidiaries, no Limerick/Raheen site entity.
gaps.detail: Mid-West presence was verified from a primary source (limerick.ie) instead.

gaps.summary: knowledge_search rejects compound, multi-clause questions with a 'too complex' message, which still costs a credit.
gaps.reproducibleQuery: knowledge_search: 'What sustainability, circular economy or community investment commitments has Analog Devices published, with document titles and years, particularly relating to Ireland or Limerick?'
gaps.detail: Decomposing into a single-clause question ('What are Analog Devices' published environmental sustainability commitments?') returned a rich, well-sourced answer.

gaps.summary: Irish grant programmes are not modelled as first-class entities (there is no funding-scheme entity type), so funding relied on knowledge_search plus primary-source verification rather than the entity workflow.
gaps.reproducibleQuery: entity_search has no entity_type for grant programmes; 'Circular Economy Innovation Grant Scheme' surfaces only via knowledge_search context.
gaps.detail: knowledge_search returned excellent, gov.ie-sourced funding detail, so the gap is in the entity model, not the underlying knowledge.

gaps.summary: Three funding facts were wrong or stale and were corrected against the funders' own pages: Aktion Mensch's maximum grant (listed as up to EUR 10,000; actually micro EUR 5,000, project up to EUR 450,000, foundation model projects up to EUR 600,000), the National Lottery Awards for All range (listed GBP 300 to 10,000; the funder's page states GBP 300 to 20,000), and the EU Social Economy Action Plan period (listed 2021 to 2026; it runs 2021 to 2030 on a nine-year horizon).
gaps.detail: The Aktion Mensch and Social Economy Action Plan errors were first surfaced by the /benchmark run, where web search and Cala disagreed with the committed data; the Awards for All figure was caught during this deadline-and-eligibility pass.

gaps.summary: Several specific budget or grant figures could not be confirmed from the funders' own landing pages and were removed or softened rather than asserted: the ESC 2026 call total (~EUR 129m), the Creative Europe 2026 budget (~EUR 396m), a CERV strand minimum (~EUR 75k), and the LIFE co-funding rate (~60%).
gaps.reproducibleQuery: WebFetch youth.europa.eu/solidarity/organisations/solidarity-projects_en; culture.ec.europa.eu/creative-europe; cinea.ec.europa.eu/programmes/life_en. None state the figure on the landing page.
gaps.detail: The figures are plausible and appear in secondary sources, but the acceptance bar is that a primary source support any specific figure. They can be reinstated once confirmed from an official call document.

gaps.summary: The top funding signals were checked for current-round status and unincorporated eligibility, but a full per-round deadline verification across all ~30 funding signals is not yet complete.
gaps.reproducibleQuery: Compare each funding signal's detail against the funder's current call page for a hard deadline.
gaps.detail: No funding signal asserts a specific future deadline; most state amounts and eligibility with an open or predictable round. The remaining national signals should be swept on the next refresh.
